editorial_thesis: The strongest fresh signal is operational: constrain agent spend, bridge identity at MCP boundaries, retire publisher super-credentials, and refresh evaluation tasks from living repositories.

topic_groups.title: Enforced Agent Economics
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Yesterday covered routing economics; today’s material update is the control plane around it: hard team/project/key caps and request-level routing evidence turn an experiment into an operable service.

sources.title: AI Gateway now supports team and project spend budgets
sources.why_selected: Moves cost control from after-the-fact reporting to enforced scope-level limits.
sources.usefulness: Give each client pilot a project ceiling and every agent key a smaller blast-radius cap.

sources.title: AI Gateway logs now have a dedicated page
sources.why_selected: A failed or expensive agent run can be explained by evidence rather than an aggregate bill.
sources.usefulness: Attach a filtered incident or client-run view to a delivery review; compare fallbacks before changing model policy.

sources.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash updated weights on AI Gateway
sources.why_selected: A silent model-weight shift is exactly the kind of material change that needs a bounded, observable re-evaluation.
sources.usefulness: Run a fixed internal coding-task set before moving this route into a client or Buildn workflow.

topic_groups.title: MCP Identity Bridges
topic_groups.selection_rationale: MCP portability was covered July 24 and stateless migration July 28; this is a specific interoperability unlock: connecting portals to SaaS MCP servers that do not implement dynamic client registration.

sources.title: Static OAuth client credentials for MCP server portals
sources.why_selected: It unlocks Slack and GitHub-style upstream MCP servers where Dynamic Client Registration is unavailable or disabled.
sources.usefulness: Publish a curated client-work portal without exposing raw upstream setup to every agent client.

sources.title: Vercel MCP now supports the 2026-07-28 MCP specification
sources.why_selected: Compatibility across client generations reduces migration pressure, but authorization behavior still needs a deliberate test.
sources.usefulness: Keep a single deployment/control endpoint available to both current and lagging internal agent clients.

topic_groups.title: Software Supply-Chain Publishing
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Recent coverage examined package malware detection; this is a distinct publisher-side credential change with a January 2027 automation deadline.

sources.title: Restricting npm 2FA-bypass granular access tokens
sources.why_selected: A leaked automation credential loses a set of account-takeover and package-control paths.
sources.usefulness: Audit Buildn/client publish secrets and separate administrative actions from release automation.

sources.title: npm trusted publishers documentation
sources.why_selected: It is the intended replacement path before bypass-2FA tokens lose direct publishing, targeted for January 2027.
sources.usefulness: Migrate a low-risk package from stored registry token to CI workload identity.

topic_groups.title: Living Agent Evaluation Data
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Agentic review and model evaluation were covered recently, but this new paper offers a different practical asset: continuously reconstructing executable tasks from an organization’s own merged PR history on healthy current bases.

sources.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
sources.why_selected: It tackles the expensive failure mode where historically real tasks no longer execute on obsolete repository states.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a Buildn evaluation corpus from merged client-safe PRs, with tests as acceptance evidence.

sources.title: Change2Task experimental HTML and resources
sources.why_selected: The numbers make a credible case for testing reconstruction before funding a manually curated benchmark program.
sources.usefulness: Use the lifecycle—healthy base → task state → restored state—as an acceptance contract for internal agent eval cases.
